remarks: RETRY OUTCOME: no improvement over the original attempt. Both previously-verified sources (NSWS home page, SPS Nellore district Inspector-of-Factories page) were re-confirmed as still live. Every one of the 13 previously-excluded URLs was re-attempted this session (most 3-4 times each, with added delays, verbose -v diagnostics on one, and a 20s timeout on the two India Code records) and every one failed again with the same class of error as before (connection reset by peer, or a 502 from the egress proxy's own CONNECT tunnel, or the same 403 bot-check on apegazette.cgg.gov.in). One new candidate (ap.meeseva.gov.in) was tried and failed the same way. verifiedSources count is unchanged at 2; excluded count went from 15 to 16 (one new candidate added, tried and failed).

Diagnostic detail gathered this retry that was not in the original: a verbose curl (-v) against ipb.ap.gov.in shows the 502 is returned directly by the egress proxy's own CONNECT tunnel ('HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway' with 'Content-Type: text/plain') before any TLS handshake with the destination even begins — i.e. the proxy itself cannot open a path to that host, this is not the destination server rejecting us. Separately, this session's own proxy-status check ('curl $HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status') independently logged 'www.aponline.gov.in:443 — connect_unreachable' and, notably, also logged unrelated failures to other states' government domains during the same run (fabkerala.gov.in, law.jk.gov.in) — evidence this is a broader egress/connectivity condition affecting many .gov.in hosts generally in this session's environment right now, not a block targeted at Andhra Pradesh specifically or a problem with these particular URLs.

spsnellore.ap.gov.in itself (one of the two verified sources) is NOT perfectly stable: of 3 consecutive re-checks this session it returned HTTP 200 twice and a connection-reset once. This confirms the original finding that connectivity to *.ap.gov.in is intermittent/flaky rather than a hard block on the whole zone, but it also means even the verified source should be understood as 'reachable some of the time' rather than reliably up, and a future re-check could plausibly catch other ap.gov.in subdomains (apindustries, labour.ap, singledesk, dof, ipb, dic, factories, goir) on a 'good' moment the way it did for spsnellore. This session's retries did not catch such a moment for any of them despite repeated attempts.

A fresh WebSearch this session for AP factory-license portals and for AP Factories Rules gazette PDFs surfaced no new .gov.in candidate URLs beyond ones already tried and excluded (apindustries.gov.in, apegazette.cgg.gov.in, labour.ap.gov.in). The only new official-looking candidate found and tried (ap.meeseva.gov.in) failed the same way as the rest. All concrete gazette/G.O. citations found via search (e.g. G.O.Ms.No.7 dated 2 March 2022, G.O.Ms.No.10 dated 14 August 2021) exist only as PDFs hosted on third-party compliance sites (compfie.aparajitha.com, simpliance.in, lexplosion.in), not on any reachable .gov.in host, so per the spec they cannot be used as sources even as citations-of-last-resort.

Conclusion: network conditions for AP government domains are unchanged from the previous attempt. The two-source verified list is accurate and current as of this retry, not stale; it is not being padded with unverifiable content. A future retry from a different network path/session, or simply trying again when the apparent broader egress issue has cleared, remains the right next step before treating apindustries.gov.in, labour.ap.gov.in and apegazette.cgg.gov.in as permanently unreachable.
